outcome: Recommend an ethical response to a security conflict and explain the duty that governs it.

sections.body: Professional ethics is more than being personally well intentioned. It constrains how security work is performed: protect society and the profession, act honorably and legally, provide diligent service to legitimate principals, and advance competence. When pressures conflict, identify the affected parties, the authority of the request, foreseeable harm, and the duty that cannot be traded away for speed or loyalty.
keyPoints: An urgent request does not erase professional duties.
Name the conflict before choosing a response.
sections.title: Ethics is a decision constraint

sections.body: An ethical response is usually concrete: decline an improper act, preserve relevant facts, use the organization’s escalation channel, and seek independent advice when needed. Do not exceed authority while trying to fix a problem. A conflict of interest, lack of competence, or request to conceal material risk should be disclosed early so an authorized party can make an accountable decision.
keyPoints: Escalation preserves accountability; it is not automatically disloyalty.
Competence includes knowing when to obtain qualified help.
sections.title: Act, document, and escalate

sections.body: The ISC2 Code of Professional Ethics supplies a professional decision constraint; an organizational code supplies local duties, reporting channels, conflicts rules, and disciplinary expectations. When they appear to conflict with speed, profit, convenience, or an instruction from authority, identify the affected public, customer, employer, and profession; preserve facts; decline an improper act; seek authorized escalation; and document the rationale. The failure mode is not only deliberate misconduct: silence, retaliation, concealed conflicts, or unreported unsafe conduct can cause harm and destroy trust. A defensible decision protects people and evidence while using the appropriate governance path.
keyPoints: Name the accountable owner, decision criterion, and evidence for each applicable outline topic.
Record the failure consequence and escalation or review trigger rather than assuming a policy label proves operation.
sections.title: Apply both professional and organizational ethical duties

summary: Ethics gives a security professional a decision boundary when a request is legal-looking, urgent, or politically popular but would compromise people, evidence, or professional trust.

assumptions: The exposure and request are confirmed facts in this hypothetical case.
The incident executive and legal channel are the organization’s authorized escalation route.
The model does not prescribe public disclosure law for any jurisdiction.

teaching.focalRelation: Executive urgency does not create authority. Maya must test authority and foreseeable harm independently, preserve the evidence, and route the decision to an accountable owner before anyone decides disclosure scope.

options.feedback: Correct. The authorized preservation remains valid while disclosure and recusal protect the independence of later decisions.

teaching.scenario: Hours before a product announcement, the product vice president tells security manager Maya to remove a confirmed customer-data exposure from the launch report. The vice president owns the launch decision, but not the risk-reporting or disclosure process. Maya has the evidence, while legal and the incident executive hold the relevant escalation authority.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The boundary model preserves independent authority and harm checks, evidence preservation, escalation before disclosure, and the changed unauthorized-tenant case. It uses authored gate states and lanes in place of the reviewed persistent duty table, so the mechanism is equivalent rather than the exact reviewed form.

workedExamples.reasoning: The manager should preserve evidence, explain the risk and applicable reporting duty, and escalate through authorized channels rather than conceal a material issue.
workedExamples.situation: A product leader asks a security manager to delay reporting a known exposure until after a sales announcement.
workedExamples.takeaway: Business pressure changes how a response is communicated, not whether material risk is handled responsibly.
